promise.statement: Semantic history accepted by a declared Kungfu domain remains identifiable, verifiable, exportable, and migratable across supported entrypoints and releases.
promise.beginsAt: one verified owner-domain success receipt with accepted status and an exact semantic identity/root
promise.endsAt: never implicitly; a successor, verified export/import recovery path, or explicit retained loss record is required
promise.scope: software continuity and verifiable portability for qualified data, not physical-media durability

owns: cross-domain compatibility, migration, loss, and GC invariants
doesNotOwn: Work, Decision, Assessment, Fact, Episode, Cut, Product Release Cut, schema, interpreter, or domain receipt semantics
transport, replication, backup, or UI session history
authority.singularityRule: Every protected member kind resolves to exactly one registry family and that family references, but never reimplements, its owner authority.
authority.receiptRule: The protection admission receipt is a verification boundary over an owner receipt. It does not replace, re-encode, or become the semantic authority for the admitted object.

retentionTaxonomy.meaning: Accepted semantic identity, roots, owner receipts, and required decoding material whose loss can strand supported user history.
Material not required for the declared success scope but retained when present and omitted only with an explicit loss record.
A read model, index, dashboard row, or presentation derived from named authority roots.
Disposable acceleration bytes whose complete reconstruction path is proved from retained authority.
Provider runtime, authentication, transport, or service state outside Kungfu semantic authority.
Credentials, private raw prompts, hidden reasoning, signed URLs, or unrelated private payloads.
Process, UI, terminal, telemetry, or provider activity that has no accepted semantic owner receipt.

beginsWhen: the member kind resolves uniquely in domainRegistry
the entrypoint routes to that domain family
the owner-domain receipt verifies under its declared schema and root
the object carries a stable identity, root protocol, and exact root
all required members and decoding roots are supported or retained
omission, redaction, and loss are explicit and do not contradict accepted status
neverBeginsFrom: an Agent session attempt without an accepted domain result
a cache, index, SQLite projection, path, timestamp, Git ref, or package SemVer alone

authority.owner: kungfu.work-control Profile over native Fact and Episode authority

domainRegistry.exportRole: Export the bounded Initiative/Assignment graph and its native Fact/Episode closure through owner adapters.
domainRegistry.migrationRule: Preserve exact native roots; a successor Profile or Work world requires explicit mapping and acceptance receipts.
domainRegistry.lossPolicy: Missing claims, reviews, decisions, assessments, or native roots make completion and continuity incomplete.

authority.owner: native Fact kernel and Episode storage service

domainRegistry.exportRole: Provide owner-verified Fact authority/Cut and full or thin Episode members.
domainRegistry.migrationRule: Use a new root protocol and mapping receipt when identity changes; never relabel an old root.
domainRegistry.lossPolicy: Unknown required record/schema/root material fails closed; explicit thin or loss state cannot claim complete continuation.

domainRegistry.exportRole: Retain the settled Cut, exact source/Atlas/Episode bindings, receipts, and portable sealed-work coordinates.
domainRegistry.migrationRule: Create a successor Cut and mapping/composition receipt; legacy roots keep their original verifier.
domainRegistry.lossPolicy: A missing semantic parent, admitted Episode, source binding, or receipt is an explicit gap and never a complete Cut.

authority.owner: Product Release Cut and Cut Transition contract

domainRegistry.exportRole: Retain exact release identity, platform slice, transition, artifact, qualification, activation, and rollback evidence.
domainRegistry.migrationRule: Move only through a verified Cut Transition; equal SemVer never substitutes for exact identity.
domainRegistry.lossPolicy: Unknown/diverged relations, missing transition roots, or cache-only rollback coordinates fail before mutation.

authority.owner: the issuing domain named by the typed receipt

domainRegistry.exportRole: Carry the exact typed owner receipt or a root-preserving evidence envelope without semantic reinterpretation.
domainRegistry.migrationRule: Preserve the payload schema and root; a new envelope or transport never changes the owner receipt identity.
domainRegistry.lossPolicy: Missing or unverifiable owner receipts remove the dependent success, migration, GC, or continuity claim.

authority.owner: each declared schema/interpreter owner composed by the portable-format authority

domainRegistry.exportRole: Retain every required schema, protocol, reader, and interpreter identity needed to verify or migrate protected members.
domainRegistry.migrationRule: Compare the complete compatibility tuple and use only declared reader or migration edges.
domainRegistry.lossPolicy: An unknown required member or decoder makes the protected scope unsupported and blocks silent copy-forward or GC.

exitComposition.role: Compose exact domain descriptors, roots, closure, omissions, loss, and capabilities without decoding member semantics.
exitComposition.fullRule: Every required member and decoder is materially present and owner-verifiable.

entrypointAuthorityMatrix.activityExcluded: command invocation, stdout/stderr, and process exit without admitted semantic output
download cache, package-manager activity, and SemVer display without exact Release Cut admission
render state, focus, navigation, and terminal transcript
renderer state, SQLite rows, view caches, and provider session state
provider authentication, raw prompts, hidden reasoning, PTY bytes, and session attempts without accepted Work
build logs, checkout caches, provider telemetry, and unadmitted task narration

compatibilityPolicy.supportedReleaseRule: A supported release preserves qualified stable data by reading it exactly, copy-forwarding it to a successor identity with a mapping receipt, or refusing before mutation.
compatibilityPolicy.supportWindow: inherits the exact released support policy; this contract does not invent an unbounded historical window

migrationPolicy.sourceRetention: retain exact source identity and bytes until successor admission and postflight equivalence verify
migrationPolicy.successorIdentity: required whenever schema, root preimage, protocol meaning, or authority changes
migrationPolicy.receipt: bind source/target protocols, roots, loss, omitted members, operation identity, and postflight result
migrationPolicy.interruption: outcome-unknown remains recoverable by exact operation/request root
migrationPolicy.unsupported: refuse before authority or source bytes change

criticalDeletionRequiresOneOf: verified equivalent successor plus successor admission receipt
verified export/import recovery path plus postflight equivalence receipt
garbageCollectionPolicy.observerDeletionRequires: verified rebuild inputs, interpreter roots, and watermark
garbageCollectionPolicy.cacheDeletionRequires: the cache is not the sole recovery input
neverDeletes: history merely because a UI, provider, installation, or package cache no longer references it

falsifiers: two registry families claim the same critical member kind
accepted status is issued from UI/process/provider activity rather than an owner receipt
required loss or omission is hidden behind a complete claim
an old identity is reinterpreted in place
a downgrade is claimed without an exact qualified reader or migration edge
recovery depends on an observer projection or cache as its only source
critical bytes are garbage-collected without an equivalent successor or verified export/import recovery path
nonClaims: No adapter or user-facing migration command is implemented by this contract slice.
No existing user home is inspected, modified, migrated, or garbage-collected.
No physical-disk-loss, backup, replication, high-availability, or infinite-history guarantee is made.
No provider credentials, hidden reasoning, raw private prompts, complete transcripts, or unbounded terminal bytes become protected history.
No current pre-release build or platform becomes release-qualified merely because this contract exists.
